verses.text: Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured Ai and completely destroyed it. Joshua had done to Ai and its king what he had done to Jericho and its king. Adoni-Zedek also heard that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them.
That frightened them, because Gibeon was as large as one of the royal cities, bigger than Ai, and all its men were strong fighters.
So King Adoni-Zedek of Jerusalem sent word to King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon.
“Come up and help me attack Gibeon. They've made peace with Joshua and the Israelites.”
The five Amorite kings, the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon, gathered with all their armies. They went up, camped outside Gibeon, and attacked it.

The men of Gibeon sent a message to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal. “Don't abandon your servants! Come quickly and save us! Help us! All the Amorite kings from the hill country have joined forces against us.”
Joshua went up from Gilgal with the whole army, including all his best fighters.
The LORD told Joshua, “Don't be afraid of them. I've handed them over to you. None of them will be able to stand against you.”
Joshua marched all night from Gilgal and caught them by surprise.
The LORD threw them into confusion before Israel and struck them down in great numbers at Gibeon. He chased them up the road toward Beth Horon and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled from Israel down the slope at Beth Horon, the LORD hurled huge hailstones from the sky on them all the way to Azekah. More died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword.
On the day the LORD handed the Amorites over to Israel, Joshua spoke to the LORD in front of the Israelites. He said, “Sun, stand still over Gibeon! Moon, stop over the Valley of Aijalon!”

The sun stood still and the moon stopped until the nation had taken vengeance on its enemies. Isn't this written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stayed in the middle of the sky and didn't go down for about a whole day.
There had never been a day like it before, and there hasn't been one since, when the LORD listened to a human voice like that. The LORD fought for Israel.
Joshua and all Israel returned to their camp at Gilgal.
The five kings had run away and hidden in a cave at Makkedah.
Someone told Joshua, “We've found the five kings. They're hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”
Joshua said, “Roll large stones over the cave entrance and leave some men there to guard them.
The rest of you keep moving. Go after your enemies and strike them from behind. Keep them from getting into their towns, because the LORD your God has handed them over to you.”
Joshua and the Israelites struck down nearly all of them in a great slaughter. The few survivors got into the fortified towns.
Then all the people returned safely to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah. No one spoke a word against any of the Israelites.
Joshua said, “Open the cave entrance and bring those five kings out to me.”
They brought the five kings out of the cave to him: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.

When the kings were brought out, Joshua called all the men of Israel and told the commanders who had gone with him, “Come forward and put your feet on these kings' necks.” They came forward and did it.
Joshua told them, “Don't be afraid or lose heart. Be strong and brave. This is what the LORD will do to every enemy you fight.”
Then Joshua struck the kings down, killed them, and hung them on five trees. They hung there until evening.
At sunset Joshua ordered them taken down. The men threw the bodies into the cave where the kings had hidden and covered its entrance with large stones that are still there today.

That same day Joshua captured Makkedah and put its people and king to the sword. He destroyed the city and everyone in it, leaving no survivors. He did to its king what he'd done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel went from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against it.
The LORD handed Libnah and its king over to Israel too. Joshua put everyone in the town to the sword, leaving no survivors. He did to its king what he'd done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel went from Libnah to Lachish, camped against it, and attacked it.
The LORD handed Lachish over to Israel. Joshua took it on the second day and put everyone in it to the sword, just as he'd done to Libnah.
Then King Horam of Gezer came to help Lachish. Joshua struck him and his people down until none were left.
Joshua and all Israel went from Lachish to Eglon, camped against it, and attacked it.
They captured it that day and put its people to the sword. Joshua destroyed everyone in the city that day, just as he'd done at Lachish.
Joshua and all Israel went up from Eglon to Hebron and attacked it.
They took Hebron and put its king, everyone living there, and the people of its surrounding towns to the sword. As at Eglon, Joshua destroyed the town and everyone in it, leaving no survivors.
Then Joshua turned back with all Israel to Debir and fought against it.

They captured Debir, its king, and its towns. They put them all to the sword and destroyed everyone, leaving no survivors. Joshua did to Debir and its king what he'd done to Hebron and to Libnah and its king.

Joshua defeated the whole region: the hill country, the south, the lowlands, the slopes, and all their kings. He left no survivors and destroyed everything that breathed, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Joshua defeated them from Kadesh Barnea to Gaza and throughout the whole region of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all these kings and their lands in one campaign because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
Then Joshua and all Israel returned to their camp at Gilgal.
